scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You open the case, and your earbuds connect before they even reach your ears. How?

scenes.name: radio
scenes.text: Bluetooth is low power radio at two point four gigahertz, the same band as Wi-Fi, but made for short distances.

scenes.name: pair
scenes.text: The first time, the devices pair. They exchange a secret key, and remember each other for next time.

scenes.name: reconn
scenes.text: After that, opening the case wakes the buds. They call out to your phone, which recognises them, and connects automatically.

scenes.name: hop
scenes.text: To dodge interference, classic Bluetooth hops between seventy nine channels, about sixteen hundred times a second.

scenes.name: codec
scenes.text: Your music is compressed by a codec like AAC, sent in tiny packets, then decoded inside the buds.

scenes.name: buds
scenes.text: Depending on the model, one bud relays sound to the other, or both listen to the phone directly, and stay in sync.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Pair, reconnect, hop, decode. Music through thin air. Follow for more on how things really work.
